nodes.name: Pyrolysis at 900°C
nodes.procedure: 300 mg cm⁻² M was sprayed on a freshly polished Co foil surface, and placed in a porcelain boat and heated at 900°C for 3 h (heating rate 5°C min⁻¹) in N₂ flow. After the temperature was naturally cool down to room temperature, the black carbon nanotube arrays peeled off automatically from the Co substrate.
nodes.source_text: the precursor was also pyrolyzed at various temperatures (900 - 1100°C).

nodes.description: ORR performance in O2-saturated 0.1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: The catalytic properties of the Co/CNFs materials toward ORR were first measured by linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) in an O2-saturated 0.1 M KOH solution... onset potential of 1.01 V versus RHE. The half wave potential (E1/2) of Co/CNFs (1000) is 0.896 V... Tafel slope (73 mV dec-1)... electron transfer number (n) was calculated to be 4.0... H2O2 yield... below 6%... negligible loss in E1/2... after 8000 cycles.

The electrocatalytic performance for OER... in 1 M KOH solution... overpotential of 0.32 V at... 10 mA cm-2... Tafel slop... 79 mV dec-1... exhibits the smallest charge transfer resistance (Rct)... largest double-layer capacitance (Cdl)... good durability.
For HER activity in alkaline... overpotential (0.19 V) at 10 mA cm-2... Tafel slop (66 mV dec-1)... noticeable smaller Rct... LSV test after 1000 cycles... chronoamperometry experiment.

nodes.description: Overall water splitting in two-electrode configuration
nodes.source_text: For overall water splitting, a two-electrode electrolyzer was constructed, simultaneously using Co/CNFs (1000) as the anode and cathode electrocatalysts... the Co/CNFs (1000) electrode cells just need a bias voltage of 1.69 V to reach a current density of 10 mA cm-2... good long-term durability... during 10 h continuous water electrolysis.

stability.value: hardly any change in voltage gap

nodes.source_text: When cycled at the current density of 15 mA cm-2, hardly any change in charging-discharging voltage gap was observed after 200 h for the Zn-air battery based on the Co/CNFs (1000) air cathode... Compared to a Zn-air battery using a Pt/C as cathode, a higher power density and specific capacity were achieved.

electrolyte.value: PVA gel with 18 M KOH + 0.02 M Zn(OAc)2

nodes.source_text: Strikingly, the solid Zn-air battery also exhibits outstanding stability without obvious performance decay.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co/CNFs (1000) film presents hierarchical structure with randomly arranged nanotubes on the surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From the scanning electron microscope (SEM) images shown in Figure 2a; Figure S2, Supporting Information, the Co/CNFs (1000) film presents hierarchical structure, in which the as-grown nanotubes are randomly arranged on the surface (Figure 2b).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co NPs are embedded in the tips of bamboo-like CNTs in Co/CNFs (1000).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscopy (TEM) image indicates that Co NPs usually embedded in the tips of bamboo-like CNTs (Figure 2c).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM displays the (111) plane of Co NPs and (002) facet of graphitic carbon in Co/CNFs (1000).
nodes.evidence_snippet: HRTEM image displays the (111) plane of Co NPs and (002) facet of graphitic carbon (Figure 2d) and the contrast line profiles are plotted in Figure 2e.

nodes.characterization_summary: C and N are homogeneously dispersed in Co/CNFs (1000) catalyst with bright Co dots in NP regions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The corresponding energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) mapping images (Figure 2f) confirm that C and N are homogeneously dispersed in catalyst. The very bright dots in the regions of NPs further demonstrated the formation of Co NPs.

nodes.characterization_summary: Peak at 26° assigned to (002) plane of graphitic carbon in CNTs; rest peaks match metallic Co phase structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure S3, Supporting Information, the peak located at 26° can be assigned to the (002) plane of graphitic carbon in CNTs.[26] The rest diffraction peaks match well with the metallic Co phase structure,[27] confirming the diffusion of Co atoms into CNFs during the carbonization process.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co loadings are 8.9 wt%, 10.3 wt%, and 13.2 wt% for Co/CNFs (900), Co/CNFs (1000), and Co/CNFs (1100), respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The actual loadings of Co were calculated to be 8.9 wt%, 10.3 wt%, and 13.2 wt% for Co/CNFs (900), Co/CNFs (1000), and Co/CNFs (1100), respectively, by inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy (ICP-AES).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co/CNFs (1000) contains Co, N, C elements; high-resolution Co2p shows Co(II) and Co(0); N1s: pyridinic-N at 398.4 eV, pyrrolic-N at 400.0 eV, graphitic-N at 401.1 eV; C1s: C=C at 284.6 eV, C-N at 285.2 eV, C-O at 286.1 eV, O=C-OH at 288.5 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution Co2p3/2 and Co2p1/2 spectra of Co/CNFs (1000) present the photoelectron signals of Co(II), Co(0), and satellites peaks (Figure 3a). The high-resolution N1s XPS spectrum shows three main peaks at 398.4, 400.0, and 401.1 ... corresponding with pyridinic-N, pyrrolic-N, and graphitic-N, respectively. For C1s spectrum ... four types of C species were observed: C = C (284.6 eV), C - N (285.2 eV), C - O (286.1 eV), and O = C - OH (288.5 eV).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co L-edge of Co/CNFs samples shows peaks at ~772 eV (L3) and ~787 eV (L2); different intensities indicate electron transfer from Co to CNTs; C K-edge: peak A (285 eV, C-C π*), peak B (C-N-C), peak C (292 eV, σ*); N K-edge: peak A (pyridinic π*), peak B (graphitic π*), peak C (C-N-C/σ*).
nodes.evidence_snippet: the Co L-edge spectra depict two separated peaks at around 772 and 787 eV, which are assigned to the L3 and L2 edges ... The different intensity of the absorption peaks is probably caused by the electron transfer from the Co to CNTs. ... the peak A at 285 eV and peak C 292 eV respond to C - C π* (ring) structure and σ* (ring) structure transitions, respectively. Moreover, peak between π* and σ* excitations (peak B) was also observed, which is associated with C - N - C. From the N K-edge spectra ... three obvious peaks can be found, which can be ascribed to pyridinic π* (peak A), graphitic π* (peak B) transitions and C - N - C or C - N σ* transition (peak C)

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge close to Co foil reference indicating Co(0) valence; FT k3-weighted EXAFS shows main peak at 2.3 Å corresponding to metallic Co-Co scattering, confirming Co nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: It is found that the Co K-edge of the Co/CNFs (1000) is close to that of the Co foil reference, which suggests that the valence state of Co in the sample should be zero. From the Fourier-transformed (FT) k3 -weighted EXAFS (Figure 3e), there is a main peak located at 2.3Å , corresponding to the metallic Co-Co scattering. This result confirms the formation of Co nanoparticles in Co/CNFs (1000) catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra show peaks at 2707, 1582, and 1355 cm⁻¹ corresponding to 2D, G, and D bands.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectra in Figure 3f; Figure S7, Supporting Information, show three remarkable peaks at 2707, 1582, and 1355 cm⁻¹ , which are corresponded to the typical 2D, G, and D bands, respectively.[35]

nodes.characterization_summary: Nitrogen adsorption-desorption curves show distinct hysteresis loop indicating typical porous nature.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The nitrogen adsorption-desorption curves indicate that the as-synthesized Co/CNFs materials possess a distinct hysteresis loop (Figure S8, Supporting Information), typical porous nature...

nodes.characterization_summary: AC HAADF-STEM reveals presence of isolated Co single atoms over Co/CNFs (1000) film.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The aberration corrected high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscope (AC HAADF-STEM) image reveals the presence of isolated Co single atoms (Co SAs) over the Co/CNFs (1000) film (Figure S13, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Near edge X-ray absorption fine structure (NEXAFS) measurements performed at Co L-edge, C K-edge, and N K-edge.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In order to investigate electronic structure, soft X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) measurement was performed.
